1	# Working in this repository
2	
3	GraphGoblin is a pnpm + Turborepo monorepo in TypeScript. Read `docs/README.md` first; `docs/12-implementation-plan.md` says what is being built now and `docs/decisions/` records settled decisions.
4	
5	## Layout
6	
7	- `packages/contracts` - Zod schemas and types. Depends on zod only.
8	- `packages/domain` - pure logic over the contracts. No I/O.
9	- `packages/engine` - executor, run manager, node handlers, written against ports. `@graphgoblin/engine/testing` has fakes for every port.
10	- `packages/infrastructure` - Node implementations of the engine ports, one folder per concern (`src/sqlite`, `src/fs`, `src/process`, `src/http`, `src/scheduler`), each with its own `index.ts` and an `@graphgoblin/infrastructure/<folder>` subpath. Folders may import each other.
11	- `packages/adapter-*` - reserved for optional external-service adapters with their own dependency (`adapter-codex`, `adapter-jev`). New packages only at real boundaries: a different runtime, reuse by several apps, or an optional or licence-sensitive dependency (ADR-0014). Otherwise add a folder.
12	- `apps/*` - composition roots: `api`, `mcp`, `web`, `plugin-codex`, `plugin-claude`.
13	- `tooling/` - shared config and the repository gate scripts.
14	
15	Layer rules are enforced by `pnpm check:layers` (declared workspace dependencies) and `pnpm check:deps` (dependency-cruiser). Reach other packages only through their `@graphgoblin/*` entry points.
16	
17	Node 22 LTS is the supported runtime; installation, development and gates need Node 22.22.2 or later, and other majors are unsupported. Select it for the whole shell before running commands. On this Windows host that is the project-scoped runtime, leaving the machine's own Node untouched: `$env:PATH = "$env:USERPROFILE\.claude\codex-runs\GraphGoblin\runtime\node-v22.23.4-win-x64;$env:PATH"` in PowerShell, or `export PATH="$HOME/.claude/codex-runs/GraphGoblin/runtime/node-v22.23.4-win-x64:$PATH"` in Git Bash. Confirm `node --version` reports `v22.22.2` or later. `.nvmrc`, CI and the container use major 22 (CI and the container take the latest 22.x); root `engines.node` and `devEngines.runtime` declare `^22.22.2`, with `onFail: error` refusing every pnpm command on an older Node 22 or another major. pnpm runs package scripts with the first `node` on PATH. Run gates through pnpm: calling `node_modules/.bin/turbo` directly bypasses this check, and Turbo's cache key ignores the running Node version. See ADR-0040 and ADR-0058.
18	
19	## Rules
20	
21	- `tooling` participates in the shared Vitest V8 coverage gate and the Turbo lint pipeline; its independent built-app acceptance suites remain separate.
22	- Every package must keep unit-test coverage at or above 90% of lines and branches. `pnpm test:coverage` fails otherwise. Do not lower thresholds or add exclusions beyond generated code.
23	- `pnpm typecheck` runs `tsc -b tsconfig.build.json && tsc -p tsconfig.json` in every TypeScript package (the web app runs `tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit`), so test files and fixtures are type-checked too; fix their types rather than casting to `any`. `tooling` is JavaScript: it has lint and coverage, not a typecheck task.
24	- Tests, lint, and typechecking need no prior build in the TypeScript packages: each lists a `development` export condition pointing at its TypeScript source, which TypeScript, Vitest, and ESLint resolve. Node at runtime loads `dist/`, so run `pnpm build` before starting an app. A new TypeScript workspace package must follow the same export-map shape. `tooling` tests drive the built API and web app: Turbo builds them first, and a direct package test needs `pnpm build` first.
25	- API subprocess tests build the API first through Turbo's `test` and `test:coverage` task dependencies.
26	- Only permissive licences (MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD, ISC). `pnpm check:licenses` enforces the allowlist in `tooling/license-allowlist.json`; add a line to `docs/research/licenses.md` for every new dependency.
27	- Relative imports use explicit `.js` extensions (NodeNext). Zod 4: use `.prefault({})` for object defaults whose fields have defaults.
28	- Keep docs in sync: a behaviour change updates the relevant numbered doc; a decision change adds an ADR.
29	- Clean design over backward compatibility, until the owner says otherwise (2026-10-04): the product is not released and has no production users. Do not build compatibility schemas, deprecated input paths, tolerant parsing of old data shapes, or dual code paths. Change the contract to its clean shape. A schema change within the current format is an ordinary Drizzle migration that keeps existing data; Drizzle migrations are for schema changes only. Stored content that a change makes invalid is never rewritten by migration code: the CHANGELOG upgrade note says which stored values to correct and how (for example the SQL), and the orchestrator corrects the owner's store by hand (ADR-0062). A change of the stored, export or device-draft format moves the current format and refuses older data clearly, with no converter, and the owner resets with `--reset` (ADR-0042); say so, and what exports or clients must change, in the CHANGELOG upgrade notes.
30	- Before picking up a GitHub issue, read `docs/15-issue-workflow.md` for its gate, routing, and delivery rules.
31	- Commits carry no assistant attribution of any kind.
32	
33	## Commands
34	
35	On Windows PowerShell, call `pnpm.cmd` (the default execution policy blocks `pnpm.ps1`); Git Bash and cmd can use `pnpm` directly.
36	
37	```
38	pnpm install
39	pnpm build
40	pnpm test:coverage
41	pnpm lint
42	pnpm docs:generate  # regenerate docs/reference after a node schema or route change
43	pnpm check          # typecheck, lint, layers, deps, coverage, licences, generated docs
44	```

# Working in this repository

GraphGoblin is a pnpm + Turborepo monorepo in TypeScript. Read `docs/README.md` first; `docs/12-implementation-plan.md` says what is being built now and `docs/decisions/` records settled decisions.

## Layout

- `packages/contracts` - Zod schemas and types. Depends on zod only.
- `packages/domain` - pure logic over the contracts. No I/O.
- `packages/engine` - executor, run manager, node handlers, written against ports. `@graphgoblin/engine/testing` has fakes for every port.
- `packages/infrastructure` - Node implementations of the engine ports, one folder per concern (`src/sqlite`, `src/fs`, `src/process`, `src/http`, `src/scheduler`), each with its own `index.ts` and an `@graphgoblin/infrastructure/<folder>` subpath. Folders may import each other.
- `packages/adapter-*` - reserved for optional external-service adapters with their own dependency (`adapter-codex`, `adapter-jev`). New packages only at real boundaries: a different runtime, reuse by several apps, or an optional or licence-sensitive dependency (ADR-0014). Otherwise add a folder.
- `apps/*` - composition roots: `api`, `mcp`, `web`, `plugin-codex`, `plugin-claude`.
- `tooling/` - shared config and the repository gate scripts.

Layer rules are enforced by `pnpm check:layers` (declared workspace dependencies) and `pnpm check:deps` (dependency-cruiser). Reach other packages only through their `@graphgoblin/*` entry points.

Node 22 LTS is the supported runtime; installation, development and gates need Node 22.22.2 or later, and other majors are unsupported. Select it for the whole shell before running commands. On this Windows host that is the project-scoped runtime, leaving the machine's own Node untouched: `$env:PATH = "$env:USERPROFILE\.claude\codex-runs\GraphGoblin\runtime\node-v22.23.4-win-x64;$env:PATH"` in PowerShell, or `export PATH="$HOME/.claude/codex-runs/GraphGoblin/runtime/node-v22.23.4-win-x64:$PATH"` in Git Bash. Confirm `node --version` reports `v22.22.2` or later. `.nvmrc`, CI and the container use major 22 (CI and the container take the latest 22.x); root `engines.node` and `devEngines.runtime` declare `^22.22.2`, with `onFail: error` refusing every pnpm command on an older Node 22 or another major. pnpm runs package scripts with the first `node` on PATH. Run gates through pnpm: calling `node_modules/.bin/turbo` directly bypasses this check, and Turbo's cache key ignores the running Node version. See ADR-0040 and ADR-0058.

## Rules

- `tooling` participates in the shared Vitest V8 coverage gate and the Turbo lint pipeline; its independent built-app acceptance suites remain separate.
- Every package must keep unit-test coverage at or above 90% of lines and branches. `pnpm test:coverage` fails otherwise. Do not lower thresholds or add exclusions beyond generated code.
- `pnpm typecheck` runs `tsc -b tsconfig.build.json && tsc -p tsconfig.json` in every TypeScript package (the web app runs `tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit`), so test files and fixtures are type-checked too; fix their types rather than casting to `any`. `tooling` is JavaScript: it has lint and coverage, not a typecheck task.
- Tests, lint, and typechecking need no prior build in the TypeScript packages: each lists a `development` export condition pointing at its TypeScript source, which TypeScript, Vitest, and ESLint resolve. Node at runtime loads `dist/`, so run `pnpm build` before starting an app. A new TypeScript workspace package must follow the same export-map shape. `tooling` tests drive the built API and web app: Turbo builds them first, and a direct package test needs `pnpm build` first.
- API subprocess tests build the API first through Turbo's `test` and `test:coverage` task dependencies.
- Only permissive licences (MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD, ISC). `pnpm check:licenses` enforces the allowlist in `tooling/license-allowlist.json`; add a line to `docs/research/licenses.md` for every new dependency.
- Relative imports use explicit `.js` extensions (NodeNext). Zod 4: use `.prefault({})` for object defaults whose fields have defaults.
- Keep docs in sync: a behaviour change updates the relevant numbered doc; a decision change adds an ADR.
- Clean design over backward compatibility, until the owner says otherwise (2026-10-04): the product is not released and has no production users. Do not build compatibility schemas, deprecated input paths, tolerant parsing of old data shapes, or dual code paths. Change the contract to its clean shape. A schema change within the current format is an ordinary Drizzle migration that keeps existing data; Drizzle migrations are for schema changes only. Stored content that a change makes invalid is never rewritten by migration code: the CHANGELOG upgrade note says which stored values to correct and how (for example the SQL), and the orchestrator corrects the owner's store by hand (ADR-0062). A change of the stored, export or device-draft format moves the current format and refuses older data clearly, with no converter, and the owner resets with `--reset` (ADR-0042); say so, and what exports or clients must change, in the CHANGELOG upgrade notes.
- Before picking up a GitHub issue, read `docs/15-issue-workflow.md` for its gate, routing, and delivery rules.
- Commits carry no assistant attribution of any kind.

## Commands

On Windows PowerShell, call `pnpm.cmd` (the default execution policy blocks `pnpm.ps1`); Git Bash and cmd can use `pnpm` directly.

```
pnpm install
pnpm build
pnpm test:coverage
pnpm lint
pnpm docs:generate  # regenerate docs/reference after a node schema or route change
pnpm check          # typecheck, lint, layers, deps, coverage, licences, generated docs
```

1	# 15 - Issue workflow
2	
3	GitHub issues are the shared work queue for this repository's development pipeline. Every non-epic issue carries at least one gate label. A triager sets the type, area, gate, QA, and routing labels from the issue and its dependencies.
4	
5	## Gates
6	
7	- `aidlc-ready`: the issue may enter this repository's agent-led development pipeline. # 15 - Issue workflow

GitHub issues are the shared work queue for this repository's development pipeline. Every non-epic issue carries at least one gate label. A triager sets the type, area, gate, QA, and routing labels from the issue and its dependencies.

## Gates

- `aidlc-ready`: the issue may enter this repository's agent-led development pipeline. Its approved behaviour is accepted through independent agent review, tests appropriate to the acceptance criteria and independent QA: tests through public methods that directly establish a criterion are sufficient for that criterion, and API, native-process or browser evidence is added where a criterion needs it. Use for bug fixes, maintainability, chores, backend work and ordinary testable feature and UI work.
- `human-in-the-loop`: the work is implemented, reviewed, tested and merged through the same agent gates, and in addition a human exercises the merged build afterwards and records what they observed. Reserve it for feature work with substantial ambiguity, or behaviour whose correctness agents cannot readily verify with confidence. A UI change does not qualify merely because it changes a screen; a missing or failing test, or a known defect, is engineering work, not a reason for the label. Before applying it, record on the issue the feature, the specific ambiguity or verification limit, what public-interface tests and other agent evidence establish, and a concrete post-merge human QA checklist with expected observations. The label does not require a human review before merge and waives no technical gate.
- `needs-plan-approval`: for architecture changes and cutovers. An agent posts a written plan as an issue comment. A human approves by replacing this label with `plan-approved` and adding `aidlc-ready`, keeping `human-in-the-loop` when it applies.
- `plan-approved`: set by a human only, after reviewing the written plan.

`aidlc-ready` describes delivery eligibility and `human-in-the-loop` describes a later human QA obligation, so the two may coexist; `needs-plan-approval` may be combined with either. Until 2026-10-21 this file described `human-in-the-loop` as a human review of the running product before merge, classified UI work under it as a whole and said it never combined with `aidlc-ready`. That wording was this repository's own metadata, not an owner requirement for objectively verifiable behaviour; the owner's clarification of 2026-10-21 (recorded in [#279](https://github.com/Jacob-J-Thomas/GraphGoblin/issues/279)) supersedes it.

## Post-merge human QA

Every pull request for a `human-in-the-loop` issue carries a post-merge human QA checklist with expected observations and names an open tracking item (the issue itself or a linked QA item). The PR references that item as "Part of", never with a closing keyword, so the pipeline never closes it. After the merge a human exercises the merged build, records the commit or build, their observations and the outcome on the tracking item, and closes it. Human QA is tracked separately from implementation, review, agent QA, CI and merge, as one of: not required, pending merge, pending human QA, or completed with an evidence link. Agent evidence never completes the human step, and the human step never permits merging a known defect or bypassing a gate. A product decision that is needed to define correct behaviour goes to the owner as a concrete question with evidence, separately from post-merge QA.

A delivery batch may carry an additional pre-merge sign-off gate (for example, a designated independent review session that must approve each PR at an exact head). Such a gate is recorded in the batch's register under `docs/delivery/` and is separate from post-merge human QA.

## Parking markers

Two labels take an issue out of the queue; neither is a gate, and an issue carrying one has no gate label until a human unparks it.

- `backlog`: parked until further notice. Agents do not plan or implement it.
- `needs-refinement`: the problem itself still needs human-driven refinement in a working session with the owner before any plan or implementation.

## QA scope

- `qa:touched-systems`: enumerate every system the change touches, test each with positive and negative cases, and record pass/fail results with evidence in both the PR and issue.
- `qa:full-regression`: also retest the whole application end to end, covering positive and negative scenarios, and catalogue the results.

Name the QA agent in the issue body's Delivery section, not with a label.

Retain QA evidence under `docs/qa/` with repository-relative citations and preserve raw JSON, YAML and JavaScript/TypeScript bytes so recorded hashes remain valid; `.prettierignore` excludes those artifacts while QA Markdown remains formatted.

## Model routing

The triager sets one `impl:<model>` label and one `review:<model>` label. Use the following tiers, with xhigh reasoning:

| Tier | Model             | Use                         |
| ---- | ----------------- | --------------------------- |
| 1    | `gpt-6-luna`      | Mundane work                |
| 2    | `gpt-6.1-sol`     | Default work                |
| 3    | `claude-opus-5.5` | Harder work and sign-off    |
| 4    | `gpt-6-astra`     | Hardest work and escalation |

Whatever model family implements the change, the other family reviews it: OpenAI models are reviewed by Claude, and Claude is reviewed by an OpenAI model. If a worker cannot finish, escalate to the next tier.

## Types, areas, and milestones

Every issue has one type: `type:bug`, `type:feature`, `type:ui-polish`, `type:architecture`, `type:chore`, `type:research`, or `type:epic`. Area labels locate the affected part of the product: `area:web`, `area:editor`, `area:settings`, `area:api`, `area:engine`, `area:contracts`, `area:design-system`, `area:templates`, `area:integrations`, `area:installer`, or `area:harness`.

Milestones are `Pre-merge #151` for work that must land before the feature PR merges, `After merge: evaluate and stabilise` for product evaluation, the architecture sweep and the cutovers they require (this milestone blocks further feature work), and `Later` for queued and long-term work, with most items parked under `backlog`.

Epics carry `type:epic` and area labels only; pipelines ignore them. Each child issue starts its body with `Part of #<epic-number>`, and the epic lists its child issues.

## Development pipeline

An issue is picked up according to its gate label. The implementer named by its `impl:` label works in an isolated branch. The reviewer named by its `review:` label reviews the diff and comes from the opposite model family. A QA agent tests according to the `qa:` label and records results in the PR and the issue. `human-in-the-loop` issues additionally get human QA of the merged build, tracked as described above. `needs-plan-approval` issues get a human-approved plan before implementation. When a human QA step is required before an issue closes (by the label, or by the owner in a comment on the issue), its pull requests reference it as "Part of" rather than "Closes", the pipeline never closes it, and the human who exercised the merged build closes it with a comment saying what was checked.

The label names and this process are specific to this repository and are not used by the product's template loops, which users run against their own repositories with their own configurable trigger label and role models (tracked in [the AIDLC template loops epic on GitHub](https://github.com/Jacob-J-Thomas/GraphGoblin/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20label%3Atype%3Aepic%20label%3Aarea%3Atemplates)).

docs/05-execution-engine.md:180:A run executes one immutable definition record for its whole life: the record its `versionId` names. Exceeding the cap fails before starting the node with `MAX_NODE_VISITS`, `resumable: false`, its node ID and `details.maxNodeVisits`. docs/05-execution-engine.md:206:resume/recovery rebuilds from what actually persisted, including an append whose acknowledgement
docs/05-execution-engine.md:227:**Child failures follow the inline rules (Decided, #251).** A child's execution error is the parent's, exactly as if the failing node had run inline in the parent; nesting adds no silent success and consumes no error. The parent fails at its subloop node with the child's failure code and resumability, the message `subloop child <id> failed: <child message>`, and `details: { childRunId, childNodeId?, childDetails? }`; its `child_run.finished` records `status: failed`. For a child with `INTERNAL_ERROR`, the copied message is the projected safe message; recognized legacy name/stack and secondary recording diagnostics are logged and not republished. Deterministic failures stay non-resumable in the parent as they are in the child. Explicitly resuming such a parent re-executes its subloop node, which resumes the same child in place (`run.resumed` with actor `{ kind: 'run', id: <parent> }`): the child's failed node runs again under the ordinary crash-recovery rules, with its thread, pins and recorded sessions intact, and no second child is started. A parent re-executed by crash recovery (not resumed) fails again with the child's failure instead of resuming the child. A child resumed directly while its parent stays failed finishes on its own; the parent's later resume then maps that outcome. Cancelling a child (operator or API) cancels the parent that awaits it, as cancelling inline work cancels its run: the parent records `run.cancel_requested` with actor `{ kind: 'run', id: <child> }` and `run.cancelled`, and its own parent follows in turn. An authored outcome is not an execution error: a child that finishes through a Failure (or Exhausted) exit returns its configured output as ordinary data, and the parent continues.
docs/05-execution-engine.md:231:**Which version a child runs (Decided, WP-G).** A `latest` reference resolves when the parent run is _created_, not when the subloop node runs. `startRun` walks every subloop reference reachable from the run's version, through the referenced loops' own subloop nodes at any depth, pins each `latest` loop to the version published at that moment, and records the map (loop id to version id) on the run's `run.queued` event as `subloopVersions`. Numbered references are immutable and need no pin, but are walked for their own references. Every child the run starts uses its pin, so a version published while the parent waits never reaches it. A child inherits its parent's pins and records them on its own `run.queued`, so a whole tree of runs sees one snapshot (it also inherits the parent's pinned model defaults, ADR-0041); every later visit of the parent's subloop node starts its new child on the same pinned selection; a replay fork copies its source's pins; recovery reads them from the log like everything else. A reference that does not resolve at creation is left unpinned and fails with `SUBLOOP_NOT_FOUND` when the child would start, as before; a run whose log predates pinning resolves `latest` when the child starts. A pinned version that is gone or no longer published fails the subloop with `SUBLOOP_NOT_FOUND`; it never falls back to latest. Deleting a loop is refused (409 `LOOP_IN_USE`) while any active run (queued, running, waiting, or paused) can still start it: a run of that loop, or one whose pins or subloop references reach it (`RunManager.loopInUse`). The check and the deletion run in one critical section with the subloop pinning in `startRun` (`RunManager.deleteLoopUnlessInUse`), together with replay-fork admission and a re-check that a new run's own version still exists, so a parent or fork created concurrently either pins the loop first (the deletion then refuses) or is created after it (and fails at that subloop like any reference to a deleted loop). A run or fork whose own version was deleted meanwhile is refused with `LOOP_NOT_FOUND`. The check reads only the first event (`run.queued`, with the pins) of each active run, plus the versions its pins reach.
docs/05-execution-engine.md:233:**A child that finishes before its parent parks (Decided, WP-G).** The parent records its `waiting/child` state after the subloop handler has started the child, so a fast child can finish while the parent is still `running`; its notification then finds no waiting parent. After the parent's park transition the run manager therefore checks the child, and wakes the parent at once if the child is already terminal; recovery does the same for every parent waiting on a child, after finalizing any child that finished while the process was down. These paths and the child's own notification go through the same identity-bound conditional append, so exactly one wins and the parent continues once. A wake that lands while the parent's executor is still returning is queued until it has returned rather than dropped.

docs/05-execution-engine.md:489:Before calling the process runner the script handler appends `script.dispatched { nodeId, visitId, dispatchId }` durably. `visitId` is `<runId>:<first node.started sequence since that node last finished>`; retries retain the visit and allocate a new dispatch ID. docs/05-execution-engine.md:491:Script failures after dispatch carry `failure.script = { visitId, dispatchId, state, exitCode? }`; the dispatch ID is absent when no durable dispatch identity exists, including an interrupted pre-change visit. A `run.failed` disposes a pending dispatch only if its script provenance matches the node, visit and dispatch. If progress or completion persistence fails after dispatch, the failure recorder preserves `SCRIPT_OUTCOME_UNCERTAIN` and that provenance instead of replacing it with a generic bookkeeping error. A known typed completed/start-failed disposition retains its class. A parent subloop failure preserves its child's typed script provenance and identifies the child run, so nested recovery exposes the same dispatch evidence. Forced stop, run deadline and unconfirmed process termination retain their non-resumable failure causes alongside the uncertain script provenance. Only explicit script-consent recovery leaves an uncertain failed run; its observed Resume knowingly retries the same visit with a new dispatch. Plain Resume refuses with `SCRIPT_CONSENT_REQUIRED`. A crash during that new dispatch is uncertain again. A crash after process exit but before recording a disposition is also uncertain. The inspector explains that the previous attempt may already have produced its effect: **Recover script** offers **Resume**, **Replay** from the failed node, and **Cancel** (leave the run failed without running anything). API and MCP return the same failure and provenance; MCP must obtain the user's explicit retry choice. No exactly-once external-effect guarantee is made; Resume or Replay may repeat an effect.
docs/05-execution-engine.md:493:**Upgrade:** no stored rewrite or migration is required. On recovery or next execution, an earlier unfinished script `node.started` with neither a dispatch marker nor an outcome is classified as `SCRIPT_OUTCOME_UNCERTAIN` before calling the runner. A first fresh entry with no earlier unfinished start can execute; absence of a marker on an already-started visit is never treated as proof that it did not run. This conservative rule also applies to a current-build crash between `node.started` and dispatch. Inspect external effects before choosing Resume (same run, fresh dispatch) or Replay (new run); either can repeat them. Cancel leaves the run failed, and leaving it failed runs nothing. Visits with a recorded completion still advance normally; an explicit retry after a recorded failure follows the disposition rules above.
docs/05-execution-engine.md:497:Wait and heartbeat handlers describe their deadlines without arming timers. The manager first appends `run.waiting`, saves its thread and parks the run; only then does it upsert the timers. Recovery completes an interrupted park from the recorded spec before arming its timers, so downtime never restarts a duration or extends a recorded wall-clock deadline. A past deadline is immediately eligible on the next poll (supported polling settings include 50 ms and 1,000 ms).
docs/05-execution-engine.md:499:Timer keys are `<kind>@<waitId>`. The opaque `waitId` combines the run ID and the durable `node.started` sequence for this park; it is recorded in the event and snapshot, rather than kept in memory. A due delivery before parking is visible returns a deferred acknowledgement: the row is conditionally requeued one configured polling interval later. A paused run acknowledges its timer without waking; resume and recovery re-arm its recorded deadline. Timers for unreadable run history are also acknowledged, leaving that history for diagnostics and explicit deletion rather than logging on every poll. This prevents deferred rows from starving other overdue timers in a full batch. The original deadline stays in the wait spec. Resume re-arms the original deadline and the next poll wakes a passed deadline. A stale timer cannot wake a later park. Wake events are conditional appends. Their status acknowledgements also compare the recorded `waitId`, so a delayed acknowledgement cannot move a later wait to running. Redelivery after a lost status response completes or queues the durable wake without appending it twice, including when the running status committed before its response was lost. The scheduler acknowledges only after all listeners accept delivery and only while the row still has the fired deadline. It also serializes same-run timer mutations and preserves any re-arm overlapping delivery, including an identical deadline on resume; an old acknowledgement cannot delete that resumed timer.
docs/05-execution-engine.md:501:After `pnpm build`, `pnpm test:wait-restart` checks observed input identities, passed deadlines, paused waits and heartbeat counts through real API process restarts at 50 ms and 1,000 ms polling. CI runs it next to `pnpm test:recovery-process`; neither command makes provider calls.
docs/05-execution-engine.md:507:- Events are appended with a monotonically increasing `seq` per run, atomically per append (several events in one append are stored together or not at all). The event store and the run record are separate writes: events go first and recovery completes the status (see "The log is written first" above).

docs/05-execution-engine.md:557:Recovery eligibility is computed once by the server and exposed as `recovery` on `GET /runs/{id}` and MCP `get_run` (ADR-0061). Both commands require the reviewed `observedSeq` and recheck this policy. docs/05-execution-engine.md:559:- Resume keeps main's status and recorded resumability rules. Paused waits keep their identity and deadlines. A completed `SCRIPT_EXIT_CODE` failure remains resumable after fixing the program. Non-resumable stop, deadline and unconfirmed-termination failures remain unavailable for Resume. A failed parent owns recovery of its exact failed child. Accepted parent recovery durably binds the child ID, failure sequence, observation and consent on `run.resumed.childRecovery`; parent ownership persists while pending. A later child failure requires new review and consent. Missing provider sessions require #265's explicit fresh-start choice for Resume; Replay remains a deliberate new attempt. It returns the same decision record read after that evidence; a raced newer record refuses as stale. Resume executes that validated status branch, so a paused node failing during validation cannot become an unconsented script retry.
docs/05-execution-engine.md:560:- Replay can start at any node the source reached, in any source status, with usable pinned definition and recorded state. It does not pause or alter the source. An active source can advance between read and command, making the observation stale. The inspector and API/MCP choice explain that scripts, provider turns, child runs and deliveries from the selected node run again for the new run. `recovery.replay[].effects` names the knowable nodes on possible paths, including loopbacks; it does not predict which branch will execute. This explanation and deliberate Replay choice provide ordinary consent. A path into the current uncertain script additionally requires explicit script consent, even if the dispatch marker is missing or Resume is non-resumable.
docs/05-execution-engine.md:562:- Fork admission atomically writes the row, initial state, first event and `(sourceRunId, nodeId, observedSeq)` intent. Migration 0024 adds nullable node and observed-sequence intent columns and a unique index using #412's canonical `replay_source_run_id`; it does not duplicate the source. A failed transaction consumes nothing. A lost commit acknowledgement finds the same admitted fork; a repeated caller receives `RECOVERY_STALE` with its exact `replayRunId`. Re-reading unchanged history does not mint another intent for that same node. New execution events give a new observation. No event is appended to the source, so terminal history, SSE completion and finalization records retain their original boundary.

470	## Resiliency model (Decided)
471	
472	Resiliency is built into the engine. Users do not model it. Failures fall into four classes.
473	
474	| Class                    | Examples                                                                                                                                                                | Engine behaviour                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
475	| ------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
476	| Transient infrastructure | SQLite busy, Jev network blip, outbound webhook 503                                                                                                                     | Internal retry with backoff, bounded, logged. Invisible to the loop.                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
477	| Harness-internal         | Model errors, tool failures inside a Codex turn                                                                                                                         | Handled inside the harness turn. GraphGoblin stops on a reported failure; explicit resume and startup recovery follow submission provenance above.                                                                                                                             |
478	| Unavoidable              | Subscription exhausted, login expired, harness not installed, working directory missing, script exits non-zero without a route, schema repair exhausted with `fail-run` | Run moves to `failed` with a typed, human-readable reason. Resume eligibility follows the cause and, for inference, the submission evidence above.                                                                                                                             |
479	| Bug                      | A handler throws anything else                                                                                                                                          | Run moves to `failed` with the safe `INTERNAL_ERROR` message, node when known, and existing resumability. Raw diagnostics go to server logs correlated by run and node when available; historical rows and events retain their earlier content. Fix the defect in GraphGoblin. |
480	
481	Provider exceptions from decision evaluation use a shared fixed summary instead of raw diagnostics. The catch-all also sanitizes errors carrying `DECIDER_*`: it stores a recognized code and the selected strategy when available, without provider messages or stacks. Engine provider warnings contain only safe name, code, numeric HTTP status, and run/node/strategy identifiers. Newly recorded ordinary internal defects expose the safe `INTERNAL_ERROR` message; their raw diagnostics are in server logs correlated by run and node when available. Historical rows and events retain their earlier content.
482	
483	Resuming a failed run re-executes the failed node using the crash-recovery rules above. A failure that came from a subloop child carries the child's class and resumability; resuming the parent resumes that child in place (see "Child failures follow the inline rules").
484	
485	### Deliberate script recovery (#321)
486	
487	The inspector follows the resumed run through its next outcome without a reload, retaining the earlier failed attempt in the timeline. Its saved event cursor advances across resumed outcomes; a historical failure does not permanently close observation of that run.
488	
489	Before calling the process runner the script handler appends `script.dispatched { nodeId, visitId, dispatchId }` durably. `visitId` is `<runId>:<first node.started sequence since that node last finished>`; retries retain the visit and allocate a new dispatch ID. A proven refusal fails with resumable `SCRIPT_START_FAILED`; ordinary explicit Resume tries it again. A completed nonzero exit retains `SCRIPT_EXIT_CODE`; timeouts retain `SCRIPT_TIMEOUT`.
490	
491	Script failures after dispatch carry `failure.script = { visitId, dispatchId, state, exitCode? }`; the dispatch ID is absent when no durable dispatch identity exists, including an interrupted pre-change visit. A `run.failed` disposes a pending dispatch only if its script provenance matches the node, visit and dispatch. If progress or completion persistence fails after dispatch, the failure recorder preserves `SCRIPT_OUTCOME_UNCERTAIN` and that provenance instead of replacing it with a generic bookkeeping error. A known typed completed/start-failed disposition retains its class. A parent subloop failure preserves its child's typed script provenance and identifies the child run, so nested recovery exposes the same dispatch evidence. Forced stop, run deadline and unconfirmed process termination retain their non-resumable failure causes alongside the uncertain script provenance. Only explicit script-consent recovery leaves an uncertain failed run; its observed Resume knowingly retries the same visit with a new dispatch. Plain Resume refuses with `SCRIPT_CONSENT_REQUIRED`. A crash during that new dispatch is uncertain again. A crash after process exit but before recording a disposition is also uncertain. The inspector explains that the previous attempt may already have produced its effect: **Recover script** offers **Resume**, **Replay** from the failed node, and **Cancel** (leave the run failed without running anything). API and MCP return the same failure and provenance; MCP must obtain the user's explicit retry choice. No exactly-once external-effect guarantee is made; Resume or Replay may repeat an effect.
492	
493	**Upgrade:** no stored rewrite or migration is required. On recovery or next execution, an earlier unfinished script `node.started` with neither a dispatch marker nor an outcome is classified as `SCRIPT_OUTCOME_UNCERTAIN` before calling the runner. A first fresh entry with no earlier unfinished start can execute; absence of a marker on an already-started visit is never treated as proof that it did not run. Inspect external effects before choosing Resume (same run, fresh dispatch) or Replay (new run); either can repeat them. Cancel leaves the run failed, and leaving it failed runs nothing. Visits with a recorded completion still advance normally; an explicit retry after a recorded failure follows the disposition rules above.
494	
495	## Timeouts (Decided minimal)
496	
497	Wait and heartbeat handlers describe their deadlines without arming timers. The manager first appends `run.waiting`, saves its thread and parks the run; only then does it upsert the timers. Recovery completes an interrupted park from the recorded spec before arming its timers, so downtime never restarts a duration or extends a recorded wall-clock deadline. 498	
499	Timer keys are `<kind>@<waitId>`. The opaque `waitId` combines the run ID and the durable `node.started` sequence for this park; it is recorded in the event and snapshot, rather than kept in memory. A due delivery before parking is visible returns a deferred acknowledgement: the row is conditionally requeued one configured polling interval later. A paused run acknowledges its timer without waking; resume and recovery re-arm its recorded deadline. Timers for unreadable run history are also acknowledged, leaving that history for diagnostics and explicit deletion rather than logging on every poll. This prevents deferred rows from starving other overdue timers in a full batch. The original deadline stays in the wait spec. Resume re-arms the original deadline and the next poll wakes a passed deadline. A stale timer cannot wake a later park. Wake events are conditional appends. Their status acknowledgements also compare the recorded `waitId`, so a delayed acknowledgement cannot move a later wait to running. Redelivery after a lost status response completes or queues the durable wake without appending it twice, including when the running status committed before its response was lost. The scheduler acknowledges only after all listeners accept delivery and only while the row still has the fired deadline. It also serializes same-run timer mutations and preserves any re-arm overlapping delivery, including an identical deadline on resume; an old acknowledgement cannot delete that resumed timer.
500	
501	After `pnpm build`, `pnpm test:wait-restart` checks observed input identities, passed deadlines, paused waits and heartbeat counts through real API process restarts at 50 ms and 1,000 ms polling. CI runs it next to `pnpm test:recovery-process`; neither command makes provider calls.
502	
503	Optional `timeoutSeconds` exists on inferencing and script nodes and on wait and heartbeat nodes through their own fields. Defaults are none. A timed-out inferencing or script node is an unavoidable failure. A timed-out wait or heartbeat follows its `onTimeout` setting.
504	
505	## Event log and projections (Decided)
506	
507	- Events are appended with a monotonically increasing `seq` per run, atomically per append (several events in one append are stored together or not at all). The event store and the run record are separate writes: events go first and recovery completes the status (see "The log is written first" above).
508	- The first event, `run.queued`, carries the run's initial thread as `initialThread`: the `run` and `invocation` blocks plus, for a subloop child, the seed the parent mapped in. Replaying `node.finished` patches over it reproduces the thread at any event without any other source (the run inspector does exactly this). Logs written before the field existed lack it; readers then start from the thread's `run` and `invocation` with empty collections. Size: the initial thread is the trigger payload (bounded by the request body limits, 8 MB for the API and 1 MB for webhooks) plus, for a child, the seed the subloop mapping selected from the parent thread; it is written once per run, next to the `runs` row's own copy, and has no separate cap in 1.0. Offloading it to the artifact store above a threshold (with a reference on the event) is the follow-up if large seeds appear in practice.
509	- The thread projection replays `node.finished` patches (a `node.finished` is applied only when it completes the open visit, the node most recently started and not yet finished; a second record of the same completion, immediate or delayed, is applied once), `decision.made` absolute gate counts, historical `iteration.incremented`, and `node.started` visit counts. **Verified checkpoints:** the executor saves the thread snapshot together with the `seq` of the event it reflects, always after that event is durable (`RunRepository.saveThread(runId, thread, seq)`, column `thread_snapshot_seq`). At every executor start it loads the checkpoint and, when its `seq` is in the log, replays only the events after it, carrying over the visit open at the checkpoint so a duplicate completion straddling it is still applied once; a snapshot without a `seq`, or one the log does not reach, is ignored and the thread is replayed from the initial thread. A run resumed after 10,000 completions replays only what follows its last checkpoint.

## Resiliency model (Decided)

Resiliency is built into the engine. Users do not model it. Failures fall into four classes.

| Class                    | Examples                                                                                                                                                                | Engine behaviour                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| ------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Transient infrastructure | SQLite busy, Jev network blip, outbound webhook 503                                                                                                                     | Internal retry with backoff, bounded, logged. Invisible to the loop.                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| Harness-internal         | Model errors, tool failures inside a Codex turn                                                                                                                         | Handled inside the harness turn. GraphGoblin stops on a reported failure; explicit resume and startup recovery follow submission provenance above.                                                                                                                             |
| Unavoidable              | Subscription exhausted, login expired, harness not installed, working directory missing, script exits non-zero without a route, schema repair exhausted with `fail-run` | Run moves to `failed` with a typed, human-readable reason. Resume eligibility follows the cause and, for inference, the submission evidence above.                                                                                                                             |
| Bug                      | A handler throws anything else                                                                                                                                          | Run moves to `failed` with the safe `INTERNAL_ERROR` message, node when known, and existing resumability. Raw diagnostics go to server logs correlated by run and node when available; historical rows and events retain their earlier content. Fix the defect in GraphGoblin. |

Provider exceptions from decision evaluation use a shared fixed summary instead of raw diagnostics. The catch-all also sanitizes errors carrying `DECIDER_*`: it stores a recognized code and the selected strategy when available, without provider messages or stacks. Engine provider warnings contain only safe name, code, numeric HTTP status, and run/node/strategy identifiers. Newly recorded ordinary internal defects expose the safe `INTERNAL_ERROR` message; their raw diagnostics are in server logs correlated by run and node when available. Historical rows and events retain their earlier content.

Resuming a failed run re-executes the failed node using the crash-recovery rules above. A failure that came from a subloop child carries the child's class and resumability; resuming the parent resumes that child in place (see "Child failures follow the inline rules").

### Deliberate script recovery (#321)

The inspector follows the resumed run through its next outcome without a reload, retaining the earlier failed attempt in the timeline. Its saved event cursor advances across resumed outcomes; a historical failure does not permanently close observation of that run.

Before calling the process runner the script handler appends `script.dispatched { nodeId, visitId, dispatchId }` durably. `visitId` is `<runId>:<first node.started sequence since that node last finished>`; retries retain the visit and allocate a new dispatch ID. The runner distinguishes `definitely-not-started` (synchronous refusal, missing command or an already-aborted request), `outcome-uncertain` (a dispatched process whose disposition is unknown), and `completed` (observed process termination). A proven refusal fails with resumable `SCRIPT_START_FAILED`; ordinary explicit Resume tries it again. A completed nonzero exit retains `SCRIPT_EXIT_CODE`; timeouts retain `SCRIPT_TIMEOUT`.

Script failures after dispatch carry `failure.script = { visitId, dispatchId, state, exitCode? }`; the dispatch ID is absent when no durable dispatch identity exists, including an interrupted pre-change visit. A `run.failed` disposes a pending dispatch only if its script provenance matches the node, visit and dispatch. If progress or completion persistence fails after dispatch, the failure recorder preserves `SCRIPT_OUTCOME_UNCERTAIN` and that provenance instead of replacing it with a generic bookkeeping error. A known typed completed/start-failed disposition retains its class. A parent subloop failure preserves its child's typed script provenance and identifies the child run, so nested recovery exposes the same dispatch evidence. Forced stop, run deadline and unconfirmed process termination retain their non-resumable failure causes alongside the uncertain script provenance. Only explicit script-consent recovery leaves an uncertain failed run; its observed Resume knowingly retries the same visit with a new dispatch. Plain Resume refuses with `SCRIPT_CONSENT_REQUIRED`. A crash during that new dispatch is uncertain again. A crash after process exit but before recording a disposition is also uncertain. The inspector explains that the previous attempt may already have produced its effect: **Recover script** offers **Resume**, **Replay** from the failed node, and **Cancel** (leave the run failed without running anything). API and MCP return the same failure and provenance; MCP must obtain the user's explicit retry choice. No exactly-once external-effect guarantee is made; Resume or Replay may repeat an effect.

**Upgrade:** no stored rewrite or migration is required. On recovery or next execution, an earlier unfinished script `node.started` with neither a dispatch marker nor an outcome is classified as `SCRIPT_OUTCOME_UNCERTAIN` before calling the runner. A first fresh entry with no earlier unfinished start can execute; absence of a marker on an already-started visit is never treated as proof that it did not run. This conservative rule also applies to a current-build crash between `node.started` and dispatch. Inspect external effects before choosing Resume (same run, fresh dispatch) or Replay (new run); either can repeat them. Cancel leaves the run failed, and leaving it failed runs nothing. Visits with a recorded completion still advance normally; an explicit retry after a recorded failure follows the disposition rules above.

## Timeouts (Decided minimal)

Wait and heartbeat handlers describe their deadlines without arming timers. The manager first appends `run.waiting`, saves its thread and parks the run; only then does it upsert the timers. Recovery completes an interrupted park from the recorded spec before arming its timers, so downtime never restarts a duration or extends a recorded wall-clock deadline. A past deadline is immediately eligible on the next poll (supported polling settings include 50 ms and 1,000 ms).

Timer keys are `<kind>@<waitId>`. The opaque `waitId` combines the run ID and the durable `node.started` sequence for this park; it is recorded in the event and snapshot, rather than kept in memory. A due delivery before parking is visible returns a deferred acknowledgement: the row is conditionally requeued one configured polling interval later. A paused run acknowledges its timer without waking; resume and recovery re-arm its recorded deadline. Timers for unreadable run history are also acknowledged, leaving that history for diagnostics and explicit deletion rather than logging on every poll. This prevents deferred rows from starving other overdue timers in a full batch. The original deadline stays in the wait spec. Resume re-arms the original deadline and the next poll wakes a passed deadline. A stale timer cannot wake a later park. Wake events are conditional appends. Their status acknowledgements also compare the recorded `waitId`, so a delayed acknowledgement cannot move a later wait to running. Redelivery after a lost status response completes or queues the durable wake without appending it twice, including when the running status committed before its response was lost. The scheduler acknowledges only after all listeners accept delivery and only while the row still has the fired deadline. It also serializes same-run timer mutations and preserves any re-arm overlapping delivery, including an identical deadline on resume; an old acknowledgement cannot delete that resumed timer.

After `pnpm build`, `pnpm test:wait-restart` checks observed input identities, passed deadlines, paused waits and heartbeat counts through real API process restarts at 50 ms and 1,000 ms polling. CI runs it next to `pnpm test:recovery-process`; neither command makes provider calls.

Optional `timeoutSeconds` exists on inferencing and script nodes and on wait and heartbeat nodes through their own fields. Defaults are none. A timed-out inferencing or script node is an unavoidable failure. A timed-out wait or heartbeat follows its `onTimeout` setting.

## Event log and projections (Decided)

- Events are appended with a monotonically increasing `seq` per run, atomically per append (several events in one append are stored together or not at all). The event store and the run record are separate writes: events go first and recovery completes the status (see "The log is written first" above).
- The first event, `run.queued`, carries the run's initial thread as `initialThread`: the `run` and `invocation` blocks plus, for a subloop child, the seed the parent mapped in. Replaying `node.finished` patches over it reproduces the thread at any event without any other source (the run inspector does exactly this). Logs written before the field existed lack it; readers then start from the thread's `run` and `invocation` with empty collections. Size: the initial thread is the trigger payload (bounded by the request body limits, 8 MB for the API and 1 MB for webhooks) plus, for a child, the seed the subloop mapping selected from the parent thread; it is written once per run, next to the `runs` row's own copy, and has no separate cap in 1.0. Offloading it to the artifact store above a threshold (with a reference on the event) is the follow-up if large seeds appear in practice.
- The thread projection replays `node.finished` patches (a `node.finished` is applied only when it completes the open visit, the node most recently started and not yet finished; a second record of the same completion, immediate or delayed, is applied once), `decision.made` absolute gate counts, historical `iteration.incremented`, and `node.started` visit counts. **Verified checkpoints:** the executor saves the thread snapshot together with the `seq` of the event it reflects, always after that event is durable (`RunRepository.saveThread(runId, thread, seq)`, column `thread_snapshot_seq`). At every executor start it loads the checkpoint and, when its `seq` is in the log, replays only the events after it, carrying over the visit open at the checkpoint so a duplicate completion straddling it is still applied once; a snapshot without a `seq`, or one the log does not reach, is ignored and the thread is replayed from the initial thread. A run resumed after 10,000 completions replays only what follows its last checkpoint.

130	runtime. Its read-only policy limits built-in tools; it does not confine filesystem reads or the
131	operating system. See [Claude Code](06-harness-integration.md#claude-code-adapter-26).
132	
133	Ports: `out`.
134	
135	## Script (Decided)
136	
137	Runs a user-written program.
138	
139	```ts
140	type ScriptConfig = {
141	  command: string;
142	  args: string[]; // args may use Liquid templates
143	  cwd?: 'workspace' | string;
144	  env?: Record<string, string>; // values may be `secret:<name>`
145	  stdin: 'thread' | 'last-output' | 'none';
146	  stdout: 'patch' | 'last-output' | 'ignore'; // 'patch' expects an RFC 6902 document
147	  exitCodeRoutes?: Record<string, string>; // e.g. { "0": "out", "3": "needs-review" }
148	  timeoutSeconds?: number;
149	};
150	```
151	
152	Behaviour: non-zero exit codes without a configured route fail the run with `SCRIPT_EXIT_CODE`, with `failure.script.state: completed` and the exit code. A proven process-start refusal fails with resumable `SCRIPT_START_FAILED` (`definitely-not-started`). Before calling the process runner the engine durably records `script.dispatched { nodeId, visitId, dispatchId }`. A dispatch without a matching recorded outcome fails with resumable `SCRIPT_OUTCOME_UNCERTAIN` (`outcome-uncertain`), including when writing progress or completion fails. A generic bookkeeping failure does not dispose the dispatch. Re-entering an unfinished script visit from an earlier build without a dispatch marker is also uncertain: missing provenance cannot prove the command never ran. Such visits never run automatically after upgrading. The previous attempt may already have produced its effect. In the inspector choose **Recover script**, then **Resume** to rerun knowingly, **Replay** to start a new run from that node, or **Cancel** to leave the run failed. Resume and Replay can repeat the effect; this is not an exactly-once guarantee (05).
153	
154	Stdout and stderr use independent streaming UTF-8 decoders, so two-, three- and
155	four-byte characters survive arbitrary subprocess chunk boundaries. Capture is
156	limited to 10 MiB of raw bytes per stream by default (`ProcessScripts.maxOutputBytes`);
157	probe callers may request stricter byte caps. A character split by a capture cap
158	is omitted; an incomplete trailing sequence at end of stream becomes U+FFFD
159	(the replacement character), including after timeout or cancellation.
160	`stdoutBytes`/`stderrBytes` count captured raw bytes before decoding, and
161	`stdoutOverflow`/`stderrOverflow` report truncation for default and explicit caps.
162	The counts exclude synthetic spawn diagnostics and replacement-character encoding.
163	Timeout and cancellation retain process-tree termination.

{"body":"Found by WP-F5 (#102 launch diagnosis) and confirmed by its independent GPT-6.1 Sol review on 2026-10-19 through the public engine interfaces. Outside every I01 to I07 bolt; filed for triage.

## Defect

A script node whose command is a Windows `.cmd` or `.bat` file (for example `npm.cmd`, bare or absolute) fails with `INTERNAL_ERROR: spawn EINVAL` instead of the typed `PROCESS_START_FAILED` result.

## Steps

1. On Windows, publish a loop with a script node whose command is `npm.cmd` (or any `.cmd`/`.bat` path) and run it.

Expected: the node fails with the typed start failure `PROCESS_START_FAILED` and the documented resumability, as it does for a missing executable.

Actual: `ProcessScripts.run` rejects with a raw `spawn EINVAL`; through the engine the run fails `INTERNAL_ERROR: spawn EINVAL`, `resumable: true`, with no normal script progress event.

## Cause

At `packages/infrastructure/src/process/scripts.ts:58`, Node's `spawn` throws synchronously inside the Promise executor for `.cmd`/`.bat` commands (Node refuses to spawn batch files without a shell), so the error never reaches the start-failure result path.

## Fix shape

Normalise synchronous start errors through the existing start-failure result path; keep `shell: false`. Explicit shell invocation by the author remains the supported way to run batch files; this issue is only about truthful failure containment.

## Related

#102 (WP-F5 record `docs/qa/2026-10-19-wp-f5-launch-diagnosis.md`), #224 (force-stop truthfulness, WP-C7).

A subloop creates a separate child run with its own version, thread, and log. The parent waits with kind `child` and continues only after the child finishes; the child's exit ends the child, not the parent, which goes on to its own next node and exit. Use **parent run** and **child runs** links to move between them. By default the parent gets `lastOutput.value` containing `status`, `outcome`, `result`, and `childRunId`; a downstream decision can branch on that status. A child whose exit returns `none` gives no `result` (the field is absent, not `null`). A child that ends through a Failure or Exhausted exit is ordinary data for the parent, which continues. ## Act on failure reasons

`SCRIPT_START_FAILED` means the runner proved the command did not start. Fix the start configuration, then Resume. `SCRIPT_OUTCOME_UNCERTAIN` means the previous attempt may already have produced its effect before its disposition was recorded. Recovery leaves it failed; **Recover script** opens an explicit choice: **Resume** runs it again in this run, **Replay** starts a new run from the failed node, **Cancel** leaves it failed. Both retry choices may repeat the effect. `failure.script` identifies the visit, dispatch, execution state and any known exit code. Completed nonzero exits still use `SCRIPT_EXIT_CODE`.

A handler failure looks like this inside the run snapshot's `failure` field:

## Inference prompt delivery

Inspect `failure.inference.submission` and the visit's `harness.turn` / `harness.submission`
events. A session ID or init announcement alone proves no prompt acceptance.

For non-pinned generic failures, Codex permits Resume even when the adapter reports
`retriable: false` for an exit or lost stream. Claude requires the adapter's `retriable`
evidence. Both still need a usable session for uncertain recovery; pinned unsupported-policy,
configuration and argument refusals remain non-resumable.

| Case                                                                                                                                                                                                         | Action                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
| Definitely not submitted (`definitely-not-submitted`)                                                                                                                                                        | Fix the external cause and Resume when eligible: the exact saved authored/repair task uses its original session selection. Unsupported policy, invalid configuration and rejected arguments need a corrected definition and a new run; the failed run's definition is pinned.                                                                                                                          
| Delivery uncertain (`HARNESS_DELIVERY_UNCERTAIN`, or a specific timeout/quota/storage cause with `delivery-uncertain`)                                                                                       | When eligible, Resume continues a usable recorded session. An inherited previous/named ID without authored-task acceptance is insufficient. When non-resumable, inspect possible effects and use **Replay from the node** for a deliberate attempt. Stop an unconfirmed native process first.                                                                                                          
| The provider refused the request (`HARNESS_TURN_FAILED` with `details.adapterCode: HARNESS_ARGUMENTS_REJECTED`; the message starts `The provider refused the request (HTTP 400, …)` and quotes the provider) | The provider refused a value the run's pinned definition sends, such as an effort or model it does not accept for this model or account. The failure keeps this cause even when the provenance says `delivery-uncertain` (Codex had already taken the prompt into its conversation). Resume is never offered, because the same request would be refused again. Correct the node, decision or default 
| Session missing (`HARNESS_SESSION_MISSING`)                                                                                                                                                                  | Preserve and inspect the failed run. Resume is refused. Use **Replay from the node** for a deliberate attempt; named-session lookup can still select the same missing conversation. To change that policy, correct the definition and start a new run. For eligible failures use the explicit Start fresh session control described below (#265).                                                      

## Find the symptom

For `SCRIPT_OUTCOME_UNCERTAIN`, the previous script attempt may already have produced its effect before its result was recorded. Recovery leaves it failed. Inspect the external system, then choose **Recover script**: **Resume** runs it again in the same run; **Replay** runs it in a new run from the failed node; **Cancel** leaves the run failed. Either retry may repeat the effect. `SCRIPT_START_FAILED` instead means the runner proved the command did not start; correct the missing command or start configuration and explicitly Resume. Nonzero completed exits retain `SCRIPT_EXIT_CODE`. The failure

After upgrading, an unfinished script visit from an earlier build may have no dispatch marker even though it already produced an effect. Recovery classifies it as `SCRIPT_OUTCOME_UNCERTAIN` with a visit ID and no dispatch ID; it does not run the command. The same failure and recovery choices remain available if writing a dispatched script's progress or completion failed. Repair the storage fault, inspect any external effect, then choose Resume or Replay knowingly, or leave the run failed with Cancel. No store reset or migration is required.

| Symptom                                                                                                                                                        | Likely cause                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | Fix                                                                                                                                                        
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
| Harness preflight says not authenticated; a run fails with `HARNESS_NOT_AUTHENTICATED`                                                                         | The selected harness login is missing or expired for the API process user.                                                                                                                                                                                                              | Run `codex login` or `claude auth login` as that user, check preflight again, and resume only a resumable failure.

| Definitely not submitted (`definitely-not-submitted`)                                                                                                                                                        | Fix the external cause and Resume when eligible: the exact saved authored/repair task uses its original session selection. Unsupported policy, invalid configuration and rejected arguments need a corrected definition and a new run; the failed run's definition is pinned.                                                                                                                          
| Delivery uncertain (`HARNESS_DELIVERY_UNCERTAIN`, or a specific timeout/quota/storage cause with `delivery-uncertain`)                                                                                       | When eligible, Resume continues a usable recorded session. An inherited previous/named ID without authored-task acceptance is insufficient. When non-resumable, inspect possible effects and use **Replay from the node** for a deliberate attempt. Stop an unconfirmed native process first.                                                                                                          
| The provider refused the request (`HARNESS_TURN_FAILED` with `details.adapterCode: HARNESS_ARGUMENTS_REJECTED`; the message starts `The provider refused the request (HTTP 400, …)` and quotes the provider) | The provider refused a value the run's pinned definition sends, such as an effort or model it does not accept for this model or account. Resume is never offered, because the same request would be refused again. Correct the node, decision or default

For eligible failures use the explicit Start fresh session control described below (#265).

For `SCRIPT_OUTCOME_UNCERTAIN`, the previous script attempt may already have produced its effect before its result was recorded. Recovery leaves it failed. Inspect the external system, then choose **Recover script**: **Resume** runs it again in the same run; **Replay** runs it in a new run from the failed node; **Cancel** leaves the run failed. Host: Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26300, Node v22.23.4 (project runtime).

## N0 raw node:child_process.spawn, shell:false (platform shape, no GraphGoblin code)

- N0-cmd-abs / N0-bat-abs: spawn() THROWS synchronously; err.code 'EINVAL', err.syscall 'spawn'
  (errno -4071 expected); no 'spawn' event; marker never appears.
- N0-cmd-upper (.CMD) / N0-bat-mixed (.Bat): same synchronous EINVAL (case-insensitive check).
- N0-cmd-trailing-dot / N0-cmd-trailing-space: synchronous EINVAL (post CVE-2024-36138 Node check);
  medium confidence. If either is not refused it is a Node platform behaviour to report, not
  forced into a PASS.
- N0-shim-extensionless (only NAME.cmd on disk, cwd+PATH contain it): async 'error' ENOENT
  (libuv searches only exact/.com/.exe), never EINVAL; no marker.
- N0-missing-exe: async 'error' ENOENT, no 'spawn' event.
- N0-cmdexe-cmd / N0-cmdexe-bat (cmd.exe /d /c <file>): 'spawn' event, exit 0, marker CREATED
  (positive control: the fixture bodies are effective when actually executed).
- N0-node-marker (node.exe -e write marker): exit 0, marker CREATED.
- Resource: the fixture process exits on its own after all cases.

## N1 ProcessScripts.run (built dist, real spawn)

- .cmd / .bat: resolves (never rejects) {state:'definitely-not-started', exitCode:null,
  stdout:'', stderr:'spawn failed: PROCESS_START_FAILED', stdoutBytes:0, stderrBytes:0,
  timedOut:false, stdoutOverflow:false, stderrOverflow:false}; no terminationUnconfirmed;
  marker absent; resolves within a few ms.
- .cmd with maxStderrBytes:0: stderr ''.
- missing exe: same definitely-not-started shape (async error path), marker n/a.
- cmd.exe /d /c refused.cmd (explicit author shell): state 'completed', exitCode 0, marker CREATED.
- node -e marker: completed, exit 0, marker CREATED.
- pre-aborted signal + node marker command: definitely-not-started without spawning, marker absent.
- Repeated .cmd refusals leave no extra active resources (getActiveResourcesInfo unchanged) and
  the process exits naturally.
- Note (source): the synthetic runner stderr still contains the token PROCESS_START_FAILED; the
  engine never surfaces stderr for definitely-not-started (no node.progress, no details).

## E engine composition (built dist RunManager + @graphgoblin/engine/testing ports + real ProcessScripts)

- .cmd/.bat script node: run status 'failed'; failure = {code:'SCRIPT_START_FAILED',
  message:'The script process could not start. Resume tries to start it again.', nodeId:'script',
  resumable:true, script:{visitId:'<runId>:<node.started seq>', dispatchId:<ULID>,
  state:'definitely-not-started'}}; no exitCode, no details; never INTERNAL_ERROR.
  Events include node.started(script), script.dispatched, run.failed; NO node.progress and NO
  node.finished for the script visit. Marker absent.
- Recovery snapshot: resume {allowed:true}; no scriptConsent; replay action for 'script' allowed.
- Plain explicit Resume (no retryUncertainScript): second script.dispatched with the SAME visitId

- Controls: missing exe -> SCRIPT_START_FAILED; node marker -> succeeded + marker; cmd.exe /d /c
